title: Reaction–diffusion
description: Paint living patterns with a Gray–Scott simulation. Compute shaders evolve two substances on a 256 × 256 grid; a separate render pass colors the result.
paint: Paint with a mouse or touch to inject substance B. Painting also works while paused.
unavailable: WebGPU is unavailable in this environment.
lost: The GPU device was lost. Reload the page to restart.
substances: Each cell stores concentrations A and B. Both diffuse to neighboring cells. Their reaction consumes A and produces B. The grid connects opposite edges.
parametersHelp: Feed replenishes A; kill removes B. The balance creates different patterns. Choosing a preset resets the same nine seeds with new parameters.
pingPong: Read texture A → compute → write texture B → swap. Each texture contains both substances. The next pass reads the newly written state; it never reads and writes the same texture.
brushHelp: The brush adds a separate compute pass before simulation: it injects B into a six-cell-radius disk, including across an edge. In pause, that pass runs without advancing the reaction.
colorHelp: Rendering maps concentration B to a palette without changing the state. Display A or B in grayscale to examine the concentrations independently of color.
speedHelp: The simulation uses a fixed numerical step. Speed selects 1–16 steps per frame, not physical seconds; evolution per second depends on browser cadence. Pause and One step let you inspect a single iteration.
